slides.title: Cooling for student hostels
slides.subtitle: CE F417 + CE F423
lines: Preference memory, building physics and constrained room control
Completed simulated research project
slides.notes: All room and occupant outcomes are simulated. The local transformer, training and exported computations actually ran. Course instructor: Prof. Rajiv Gupta.

slides.title: Research question
lines: Can retained student preferences guide fan, window and curtain decisions?
F417: language, memory and AI comparisons
F423: airflow, solar gains and energy
Study, sleep and away can require different settings
slides.notes: Source proposals define the combined scope. Conversation-based comfort learning already exists: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enbuild.2026.117181

slides.title: Implemented system
lines: 1. Consented feedback updates an activity-specific profile
2. Heat and moisture balances estimate room conditions
3. Fuzzy comfort and a GA score legal controls
4. Suggestions, evidence and self-reports persist locally
Learned activity inference and CSV calibration are available in the application
slides.notes: Source: implemented modules preferences.py, physics.py, optimizer.py, server.py and routines.py. Self-reports remain separate from simulation labels.

slides.title: Room model and calibration
lines: C dT/dt = G (Tout - T) + solar + internal gains + fan power
Fan electrical heat and perceived airflow relief remain separate
slides.notes: The fitted parameters use separate noisy observations and can be biased. Model structure context: https://energyplus.readthedocs.io/en/stable/guides/engineering-reference/2.1-basis-for-the-zone-and-air-system-integration.html

slides.title: Actual local preference learning
lines: Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M
Pinned model revision and SHA256; local inference, no API key
Structured values require exact-message evidence quotes
Separate study and sleep targets survive activity changes
Invalid values and unsupported evidence cannot silently change memory
slides.notes: Model source: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-4B-GGUF. Inference API: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md. Actual prompts and outputs: llm_inference.jsonl.

slides.title: Saved learning models
lines: Comfort ANN: 0.148 TSV holdout MAE
2,000 training and 400 independent synthetic holdout points
Routine model: 93.5% chronological test accuracy
Majority routine baseline: 36.6%
Saved weights, counts, datasets and validation metadata accompany the project
slides.notes: All model validation labels are synthetic. Routine split: 14 train days and seven later test days. Source: models/ann_validation.json and routine_validation.json.

slides.title: Matched experimental design
lines: 7 days per seed; seeds [11, 23, 47]
15-minute physics, hourly control decisions for every policy
9 methods, separate closed-loop room trajectories
Same forcing, initial state and explicit constraints
Survey and no-physics ablations isolate memory and lookahead
slides.notes: All actions apply, including proxy-declined suggestions. Comfort excludes away intervals. The generic LLM receives no personal history or numerical room forecast.

lines: Synthetic comfort outcomes; actual generic LLM inference
slides.notes: Source: CE_F417_comparison.csv. Adaptive reference uses a documented fallback outside awake/study applicability. https://pythermalcomfort.readthedocs.io/en/latest/documentation/models.html

slides.title: F423 fan electricity
lines: Energy must be interpreted alongside occupied discomfort
Proposed period fan EPI: 0.1696 kWh/m2
slides.notes: Source: CE_F423_comparison.csv. EPI covers only fan electricity during this trial, not annual whole-building EPI.

slides.title: Comfort and energy trade-off
lines: Ours: 290.7 Wh/day; 54.7% violations
Fixed: 448.0 Wh/day; 52.3% violations
Fan energy change: -35.1%
Comfort violation change: +2.38 percentage points
Synthetic results establish a scenario trade-off, not a human benefit
slides.notes: Source: summary.json and paired_comparisons.csv. Paired weather-seed intervals are exploratory with n=3; no participant inference.

lines: The survey starts with the same initial profile
A scripted target change reaches only memory-enabled policies
slides.notes: Source: comparison.csv and conversation_evidence.json. The small scripted experiment tests retention mechanically; it is not an actual conversation-versus-survey trial.

slides.title: Language evaluation
lines: 24 fixed held-out synthetic phrases
Exact-match accuracy: 70.8%
Field precision / recall: 0.667 / 0.800
Cross-activity persistence: True
All failures and safe rejections remain in the evidence
The app requires review and confirmation before saving preferences
slides.notes: Source: language_evaluation.json. This is real local model inference, not parser output. Phrases include negation, unrelated observations, invalid values and mixed contexts.

slides.title: Held-out room prediction
lines: 14 days of noisy synthetic observations
Chronological 80/20 transition split
Low prediction error does not prove parameter identifiability
slides.notes: Source: calibration.json and noisy_pilot_metadata.json. Parameter selection never uses test transitions.

slides.title: Objective-weight sensitivity
lines: Six declared weights; three seeds and three days per weight
Comfort outcomes accompany the energy curve in sensitivity.csv
slides.notes: This sweep illustrates objective dependence. It does not select a winning weight after observing the test outcomes.

slides.title: F417 hypothesis findings
table: Mechanism supported in scripted cases; broader claim untested
3/3 changed study targets exactly recovered. Unchanged survey target error: 1 C after the change.
Supported on the synthetic routine holdout
Supported by the assumed acceptance proxy
Ours minus survey: +4.76 percentage points across the trial; +9.70 after the scripted change.
Versus fixed: fan energy -35.11%; occupied violations +2.38 percentage points.
slides.notes: Original proposal hypotheses assessed against recorded synthetic outcomes. F417 H1: Explicit numeric messages do not measure natural conversational coverage or survey burden. F417 H2: Synthetic schedules; no student routine was observed. F417 H3: Acceptance is a simulated occupant rule. Every suggested action applies regardless of acceptance. F417 H4: No human non-inferiority margin or powered field study was conducted.

slides.title: F423 hypothesis findings
table: Fan energy decreases, but discomfort violations increase by 2.38 percentage points versus fixed.
Activity targets persist across context switches; away intervals use fan off; sleeping obeys the configured fan maximum.
Supported for discomfort under the no-physics ablation
Ours minus no-physics: occupied violations -16.44 percentage points; fan electricity +145.7 Wh/day.
Supported for the trial-period fan EPI
Ours 0.1696 versus fixed 0.2613 kWh/m2 over the seven-day period (-35.11%).
slides.notes: Original proposal hypotheses assessed against recorded synthetic outcomes. F423 H1: The lower electricity outcome includes a comfort trade-off. F423 H2: The main controller trial uses observed synthetic activity. Learned auto mode is evaluated separately. F423 H3: Lookahead improves modeled comfort at higher energy. This is a joint policy comparison, not a proof of physical accuracy. F423 H4: Fan-only period EPI excludes lighting, appliances and other building electricity. It is not annual whole-building EPI.

slides.title: Completed deliverables
lines: Working local application with actual transformer requests
Saved ANN and routine models, plus material and calibration tools
Both course baseline sets, ablations and sensitivity analysis
Raw interval data, inference journals and automated checks
Reproducible setup, complete report and source repository
slides.notes: The approved scope is a completed simulated course project. Physical sensors, metered human outcomes and a 20-50 room field study are separate empirical work.

slides.title: Limits and interpretation
lines: One-node room physics omits radiant and spatial effects
Comfort labels and acceptance derive from assumed synthetic occupants
LLM extraction can miss or misinterpret phrases
No human effectiveness or building-certification claim
A measured, consented field study would test external validity
slides.notes: Preserve the distinction between completed software and unmeasured real-world benefit. The project reports unfavorable outcomes instead of manufacturing positive hypotheses.
